 J U D G M E N T
This petition under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act, 1989 is filed seeking compensation for the death of Sri.H.Anand S/o Hariyappa M.R. in a road traffic accident.

2. It is stated in the petition that on 27012023 about 8.45 p.m. H.Anand was walking on the extreme left side of Mariyaladahundi gate, Chamarajanagar - Nanjangudu road, Chamarajanagar, at that time, all of a sudden, the driver of a Car bearing No.KA10P5050 (herein after called as offending vehicle) drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against Anand from behind.
Due to the impact, Anand fell down and sustained severe injuries all over the body and died on the spot.

Later postmortem was conducted at District hospital,
Chamarajanagar and then dead body was handed over to the Petitioners and they have performed his last rites.
3. It is stated that the accident and death was due to negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.
The deceased was aged about 48 years, he was working as a Coolie and earning 30,000/ p.m.

The Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioner No.2 is the daughter of deceased and they were depending upon the income of deceased and due to untimely death of Anand, they have suffered mental shock and agony and lost their bread earner of the family.

As the Petitioners have spent 1,50,000/ for transportation of dead body, funeral and other expenses also, it is requested to award 50,00,000/
compensation with interest from the Respondent No.2 and 3 being the insured and insurer of the offending vehicle.
4. After service of notice, respondent No.1 deleted by the petitioners, finding that the respondent No.1 issued only temporary permit to said vehicle.
The Respondents No.2 and 3 have appeared before the court through their counsel and resisted the petition by filing objections.
5. The Respondent No.2owner has filed objections by denying all the petition averments.
He has denied the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending car, on the other hand the accident has occurred due to negligence of deceased himself.

Further, 2nd Respondent is the RC owner of the offending vehicle and same was insured with Respondent No.3 and policy was in force at the time of Triveni.S vs Icici Lomb Gen Ins Co Ltd on 14 June, 2024

Hence, the Respondent No.3 insurer is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners and prayed for dismissal of the petition against him.
6. The Respondent No.3Insurance Company in its objections has admitted the issuance of insurance policy in respect of offending vehicle and its validity as on the date of accident.
However its liability is subjected to terms and conditions mentioned in the policy.
It has contended that that the owner of the offending vehicle has not complied the mandatory provisions of Sec.134(C) of MV Act.
Further it has denied the involvement of offending vehicle in the accident and also the manner of accident.

Further it has contended that the accident has occurred due to negligence of deceased himself as he was walking on the road without having proper look after the coming vehicles and as such there is no negligence on the part of driver of car.
Further it has contended that the driver of offending vehicle had no valid DL and the driver of offending car is also proper and necessary party for adjudication of the case.

It has denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased,
relationship of petitioners and their dependency and contended that compensation claimed is highly excessive and exorbitant and prayed for dismissal of the petition.

7. On the basis of above pleadings, the following issues have been framed :-
1.

Whether the Petitioners prove that the death of H.Anand S/o.Hariyappa M.R. was only due to rash and negligent driving by the driver of Car bearing No.KA10P 5050 on 27012023, about 8.45 p.m. Mariyaladahundi Gate, Chamarajanagar Nanjanagudu Road, Chamarajanagar District?

2. What compensation Petitioners are entitled?
3. What order?

sentences.text: 12 . ISSUE NO.1:

Petitioners say that on 27012023 about 8.45 p.m. H.Anand was walking on the extreme left side of Mariyaladahundi gate, Chamarajanagar - Nanjangudu road, Chamarajanagar, at that time, all of a sudden, the driver of a Car bearing No.KA10P5050 drove the same with high speed, in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against Anand from behind.

Due to the impact,
Anand fell down and sustained severe injuries all over the body and died on the spot.
Petitioners say that it was the negligence of the driver of the offending vehicle.

They relied on the police records and submitted that the police have filed charge sheet against the driver of the offending vehicle and it is requested to award compensation from the owner and the insurer of the offending vehicle.
13. In support of their version Petitioners have produced FIR, Complaint, seizure mahazar, spot sketch, PM report, Inquest report, IMV report, notice, reply and Charge sheet at Ex.P.1 to 10.
All the police records supports the contention of the petitioners.

Petitioners have stated that it was the negligence only on the part of driver of alleged offending vehicle who drove the car in a rash and negligent manner and dashed to the Anand and caused the accident.

14. To prove the negligence on the part driver of the alleged offending vehicle, 1st Petitioner examined herself as PW1 who has stated that on the alleged date, time and place her husband had met with an accident and succumbed to the injuries and the alleged accident occurred due to negligence of driver of offending vehicle.
She is not an eyewitness and she relied on the police records.

15. The insurance company has contended that the deceased himself was negligent and during crossexamination it was suggested to PW1 that the accident took place due to the negligence of her husband as he came in the middle of the road.
She denied that her husband was negligently walking on the road and due to his negligence the accident took place and there was no negligence on the part of driver of car.
16. Respondents have not challenged the chargesheet filed against the driver of car.
There are no material to over come the finding in the chargesheet.
Petitioners have proved that the death of Anand was only due to the rash and negligent driving of driver of offending car.
Hence, this issue is answered in the Affirmative.

17. ISSUE NO.2: With regarding the quantum of compensation and liability, following citation followed:
(2017) 16 SCC 680: (2018) 2 SCC (Cri) 205: (2018) 3 SCC (Civ) 248: 2017 SCC OnLine SC 1270 the Honourable Supreme Court of India, in NATIONAL INSURANCE COMPANY LIMITED Versus PRANAY SETHI AND OTHERS..

sentences.text: In regard to bachelors, normally, 50% is deducted as personal and living expenses, because it is assumed that a bachelor would tend to spend more on himself.
Even otherwise, there is also the possibility of his getting married in a short time, in which event contribution to the parents) and siblings is likely to be cut drastically.
Further, subject to evidence to the contrary.

the father is likely to have his own income and will not be considered as a dependant and the mother alone will be considered as dependant in the absence of evidence to the contrary, brothers and sisters will not be considered as dependents, because they will either be independent and earning.
or married, or be dependent on the father.

32. Thus even if the deceased is survived by parents and siblings, only the mother would be considered to be a dependant,and 50% would be treated as the personal and living expenses of the bachelor and 50% as the contribution to the family.

However, where the family of the bachelor is large and dependent on the income of the deceased, as in a case where he has a widowed mother and large number of younger non earning sisters or brothers, his personal and living expenses may be restricted to onethird and contribution to the family will be taken as twothird."

(2) On grant of loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses Reasonable figures on conventional heads, namely, loss of estate, loss of consortium and funeral expenses should be Rs 15,000, Rs 40,000 and Rs 15,000 respectively.
The aforesaid amounts should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
(3) On addition of future  prospects to determine the
multiplicand We determining the income

, an addition of 50% of actual salary to the income of the deceased towards future prospects, where deceased had a permanent job and was below the age of 40 years,

sentences.text: The addition should be 30% if the age of the deceased was between 40 to 50 years.
In case the deceased was between the age of 50 to 60 years, the addition should be 15%.
Actual salary should be read as actual salary less tax.
In case the deceased was selfemployed or on a fixed salary, an addition of 40 % of the established income should be the warrant where the deceased was below the age of 40 years.
An addition of 25% where the deceased was between the age of 40 to 50 years and 10% where the deceased was between the age of s0 to 60 years should be regarded as the necessary method of computation.
The established income means the income minus the tax component.
Petitioners states that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Anand.
The Petitioner No.1 is the wife and Petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased.
They have produced the Aadhaar cards, which clearly indicates that deceased is the husband of first Petitioner Petitioner No.2 is the daughter of the deceased.
Hence, I hold that the Petitioners are the legal representatives of the deceased and they are entitled for compensation as dependents.
18. It is stated that the deceased was 48 years old and was working as a coolie and earning .30,000/ p.m. and was the sole earning member of the family.
In order to show the avocation and income of the deceased Petitioners have not produced any supportive documents.

Considering the age of the deceased and the date of accident and in the absence of proof of income, notional income of .16,000/ per month is taken as per Lokadalath settlement of MVC cases SOP issued by Hon'ble KSLSA, Bengaluru.
19. According to the ExP14 Aadhar card, the date of the birth of deceased is mentioned as 1910 1974.
Ex.P.5PM report shows that age of the deceased as 48 years.
As per these documents his age was 4849 years as on the date of accident and same is considered.
As per the age of the deceased the proper multiplier applicable to the case on hand is 13 as per the Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation.

As there are 2 dependents, as per the decision of Hon'ble Supreme Court in Sarla Verma Vs. Delhi Transport Corporation reported in 2009 ACJ 1298 1/3rd of the income to be deducted towards his personal and living expenses and then the annual income would come around .13,333 x 12 =
.1,59,996/ and by applying 13 multiplier, the loss of dependency would be .20,79,948/.

Liability:
As it is already held in issue No.1 that it was the negligence on the part of the driver of the offending vehicle in causing the accident, which was insured with Respondent No.3  insurance company.
Hence, the Respondents No.2 and 3 are jointly and severally liable to pay the compensation.
The policy was in existence as on the date of accident and hence Respondent No.3 insurance company is liable to indemnify the claim of the Petitioners with interest @ 6% p.a.
With these observations, I have answered Issue No.2 partly in the affirmative.
